analysis:
Documentation-only changes. docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md (head 154 adoption end condition; head 175-212, 278-281, 293-297) adds a selected-model recovery description. Recovery requeues operator-selected models that an Autopilot operation unloaded, and may evict an adopted, unheld slot after victim rules (min_dwell, lease, idle threshold, a 10-minute release delay). It never evicts the ordinary selection, pins, held slots or models a request could reload, and an add-on hold pauses or cancels it (enterAddonHold). Released adoptions are withdrawn, refuse new requests as model_not_selected, and let in-flight requests finish.

Security relevance is availability and routing (A-018, TB-012/T-059). The behavior favors operator selection over coordinator placements; it grants no new authorization, attestation, encryption or billing path. Recovery reports busy as preload, so concurrent operations are refused.

Units d25347f864a05087:5-6 (head 446-881) are unchanged context beyond the head 371-408 recovery paragraph, which is outside the supplied text. Its excerpt mirrors the autopilot doc: allowEviction:false, isProtectedFromRecoveryEviction and evictionExclusions. No memory-cap or T-041 cache semantics change is described.

The implementation source (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift, ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift) was not supplied, so whether it matches these documented guards remains unverified. Integration should check whether the code that releases an adoption while requests are in flight preserves native retirement and memory ownership as the doc claims. No regression is identified from the docs alone.
